excerpts.author: fradamt
excerpts.content:
The whole crList thing is in combination with PBS, which comes with (block, slot) attestations, meaning you can vote against block B at slot n by voting for its parent A from slot n-1, but at slot n (e.g. attest to (A, n) instead of (B,n)).  What that means then is that a builder at slot 2n+3 which does not comply with the crList from the previous proposer (the one from slot 2n) can have their block voted out of the fork-choice. 
The reason to have the list be made by the previous proposer (rather than the one from 2n+2, I.e. the one which has chosen this builder) is that this way there is 0 reason to not make a crList or to be careful about what you put in it, at least in terms of profits (of course you might be worried  about legal repercussions of making a certain kind of list, but we can’t do anything to prevent that)

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Ah, I see.  So "vote **against**" here means to vote for a *different* block to be in that slot.  I didn't realize that was planning to be an option.  Thanks!

excerpts.author: fradamt
excerpts.content: Yes. Currently it’s not an option because voting for the parent A of block B also contributes fork-choice weight to B (B always dominates A in the fork-choice), so you can’t vote for excluding something from the chain

excerpts.author: fradamt
excerpts.content: Generally, this allows any kind of “committee-enforceable property”, meaning attempting to use “voting against” to enforce things which cannot be done with validity conditions (e.g. timing requirements)

I just took a quick look but I believe the censorship, if it exists, will happen in two places neither of which are in the relay code.
1) Flashbots block builder
      a) They don't accept censored transactions into their private mempool - not so bad

2) Their simulator, which is checked by the relay but not in the relay code, won't validate blocks with censored transactions - very very bad
